name: Menien
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.note: Page does not exist (404); no Menien bibliography there.
No descriptive references; only Silva Martins 2007, Martius 1867 and Métraux 1930 cited for classification/existence.

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. PhD thesis, Universidade de Brasília. p. 23.
sources.note: 'Apenas uma lista, da autoria de Wied-Neuwied ([1820] 1940, p. 490–491), está disponível para a língua dos Menien[meni1247], do rio Jequitinhonha'; Kamakã phonology not treated.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri, Valdir Vegini & Maria Cristina Victorino de França. 2015. Koropó, puri, kamakã e outras línguas do Leste brasileiro: revisão e proposta de nova classificação. LIAMES 15(2): 223-277. doi:10.20396/liames.v15i2.8642302.
sources.note: pp. 250-251: '(Me) †Menien (Wied-Neuwied 1989: 513-514) [1816]', Menien intermediate between Kamakã and Masakará; Anexo III Menien column. p. 237: the 19th-c. accents 'não vem acompanhado da devida explicação sobre os seus significados'. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Martins, Andérbio Márcio Silva. 2007. Revisão da família lingüística Kamakã proposta por Chestmir Loukotka. MA thesis, Universidade de Brasília. 89 pp.
sources.note: Menien data = 'Me – Menien (Wied)'; pp. 17-18 ethnohistory; ch. 4 segmental correspondences (Kamakã (t)ʃ : Menien j, *h ~ zero). No 'acento'/'tônica' anywhere; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Métraux, Alfred & Curt Nimuendajú. 1946. The Camacan linguistic family. HSAI vol. 1: 547-552; Étienne, Ignace. 1912. Les Camacans. Anthropos 7: 948-956.
sources.note: Ethnographic only (Menian = Camacan refugees at Villa de Belmonte who in 1817 'hardly remembered their native language'; Étienne's 'menien' vocabulary is a plagiarism per Loukotka). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1932. La familia lingüística Kamakan del Brasil. Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán 2: 493-524.
sources.note: p. 497 source list: 'Me.: Menien. WIED.. páginas 325-326, traducción francesa, páginas 352-355'; pp. 496-497 show Guimarães's and Étienne's 'menien' vocabularies to be plagiarised retranslations of Wied. Fonética p. 498 only: 'Las vocales acentuadas están indicadas por un acento'. No stress rule.

sources.citation: Martius, C. F. P. von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, I. Zur Ethnographie. Leipzig: Fleischer. p. 345.
sources.note: Ethnographic: the Meniens of Villa de Belmonte 'hatten ihre Sprache verlernt, so dass nur noch einige Alte derselben eines theilweise sehr abweichenden Rothwälsch mächtig waren'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1863. Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium. Erlangen: Junge (= Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens II, 1867). 'MENIENS', p. 155.
sources.note: Latin-glossed reprint of Wied's list keeping Wied's acutes; footnote: 'Aus Neuwied Reise II. 324. Dieses Rothwälsch hat wahrscheinlich auch Worte aus den Idiomen der Neger, mit denen vermischt die Meniens leben, aufgenommen. Vergl. oben I. 345.' Only the book-wide p. 29 key (acute 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen', written about Tupi). No Menien stress statement.

sources.citation: Wied-Neuwied, Maximilian Prinz zu. 1850. Brasilien. Nachträge, Berichtigungen und Zusätze zu der Beschreibung meiner Reise im östlichen Brasilien. Frankfurt a. M.: Brönner.
sources.note: 'Einige berichtigende Bemerkungen zu den Sprachproben' (pp. 140 ff.) correct Botocudo forms only; the note to II p. 214 on the Camacans is ethnographic; the Marica note (p. 8) shows Wied uses 'Accent' for the stressed syllable in general. Nothing on Menien stress.

sources.citation: Wied-Neuwied, Maximilian. 1822. Voyage au Brésil, dans les années 1815, 1816 et 1817, t. III (French translation; Menien list pp. 352-355 per Loukotka 1932).
sources.note: Only to check whether the translator added an accent key; unlikely to supersede the German original already read.

sources.citation: Wied-Neuwied, Maximilian Prinz zu. 1821. Reise nach Brasilien in den Jahren 1815 bis 1817, Bd. 2. Frankfurt a. M.: Brönner. II. Sprachproben, '6) Sprachproben der civilisirten Camacan-Indianer zu Belmonte, welche von den Portugiesen Meniens (deutsch etwa Meniengs) genannt werden', pp. 325-326; main text pp. 213-214; notation key pp. 303-305.
sources.note: The sole primary record: c. 95 German-glossed items. Anmerkung p. 325: 'Diese Sprache hat mehrere Gaumen- und besonders Nasentöne, auch werden die Worte im Allgemeinen für den Fremden sehr undeutlich ausgesprochen.' Per-word remarks only; the single explicit accent note is 'Heute, Ínu (i der Accent)'. Most forms carry an acute on the final vowel (Imgutó, Jundú, Jucuá, Sacré, Tuwuá, Iniatagó, Camajó, Tamanduá.; exceptions Ínu, Ingóte), but the general key pp. 303-305 never defines the acute, and pp. 213-214 warn that only a couple of old people still knew the language and the forms are 'nicht…

sources.citation: Wied-Neuwied, Maximiliano. 1940 [2nd ed. 1958]. Viagem ao Brasil (trans. E. S. de Mendonça & F. P. de Figueiredo; Brasiliana 1). São Paulo: Companhia Editora Nacional. Menien list pp. 490-491 (Nikulin) / 513-514 (Ramirez).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The edition modern Brazilian comparativists cite; any editorial note on the accents would be here. Not on archive.org.

tone.summary: Wordlist only; no statement on tone or stress. Nota (p. 490): 'Ha nesta lingua muitos sons palatais e especialmente nasais..'. Acute accents (mostly on final vowels) are printed with no key.
